questions.text: I'm just not smart enough to succeed at difficult things
Some people are naturally talented — I'm not one of them
I can't learn new skills easily; my brain doesn't work that way
If I haven't figured something out quickly, I probably never will
I'm not creative — I can't think of original ideas
I don't deserve success because I haven't worked hard enough
Good things happen to other people, not to me
If people really knew me, they wouldn't respect me
I'm not the kind of person who achieves big things
I feel guilty when something good happens to me
If I try and fail, people will think less of me
It's better not to try than to try and fail publicly
Failure means I'm a failure as a person
I avoid challenges because I might not be good enough
Making mistakes proves that I'm not capable
People don't really change — you either have it or you don't
My past defines my future — I can't break free from it
Hard work won't help if you don't have natural ability
I've always been this way and I always will be
Successful people were born lucky — effort alone won't get me there
I often tell myself 'I can't do this' before even trying
When something goes wrong, my first thought is 'I knew it — I always mess up'
I replay my mistakes in my head over and over
I focus more on what went wrong than what went right
My inner voice is more critical than encouraging

bands.label: Moderate — Some Beliefs Holding You Back

Ability.label: Beliefs About Ability
Ability.low: You believe in your capacity to learn and grow. You see ability as something that develops with effort.
Ability.moderate: You sometimes doubt your abilities. Remember: intelligence is not fixed — every expert was once a beginner.
Ability.high: You strongly believe your abilities are limited. This belief itself is the biggest barrier. Research proves that brains grow with practice — you CAN learn anything with effort and time.
Ability.reframe: Instead of 'I'm not smart enough', try 'I haven't learned this YET'.

Worthiness.label: Beliefs About Worthiness
Worthiness.low: You feel deserving of success and good things. You know your worth.
Worthiness.moderate: You sometimes question whether you deserve good outcomes. You are worthy simply because you exist — success is not reserved for 'special' people.
Worthiness.high: You carry a deep belief that you're not worthy of success. This is a learned belief, not a fact. You deserve every good thing that comes your way.
Worthiness.reframe: Instead of 'I don't deserve this', try 'I am worthy of good things because of who I am, not just what I do'.

Fear of Failure.label: Fear of Failure
Fear of Failure.low: You see failure as a learning opportunity, not a judgment of your worth. This is a powerful mindset.
Fear of Failure.moderate: Failure feels uncomfortable for you. That's normal — but remember, every successful person failed many times before succeeding.
Fear of Failure.high: Fear of failure is strongly holding you back. You avoid risks to protect yourself. But avoidance guarantees one thing: you'll never know what you're capable of.
Fear of Failure.reframe: Instead of 'What if I fail?', try 'What if I learn something valuable?'.

Fixed Mindset.label: Fixed Mindset Beliefs
Fixed Mindset.low: You have a growth mindset — you believe people can change and improve. This is scientifically accurate.
Fixed Mindset.moderate: You partially believe things are fixed. In reality, neuroscience proves your brain creates new connections every time you practice something.
Fixed Mindset.high: You strongly believe people can't change. This is the most limiting belief of all — because if you believe you can't grow, you won't try. But science says otherwise: neuroplasticity is real.
Fixed Mindset.reframe: Instead of 'I've always been this way', try 'I'm choosing to grow in a new direction'.

Negative Self-Talk.label: Negative Self-Talk
Negative Self-Talk.low: Your inner voice is mostly encouraging and balanced. You're kind to yourself.
Negative Self-Talk.moderate: Your inner critic is active. Start noticing when it speaks — awareness is the first step to changing the conversation.
Negative Self-Talk.high: Your inner voice is harshly critical. You speak to yourself in ways you'd never speak to a friend. This constant negativity drains your energy and confidence. Practice replacing one negative thought per day with a neutral or kind one.
Negative Self-Talk.reframe: Instead of 'I always mess up', try 'I'm learning and that's okay'.
